title: Existing Insulin Pump Program Payment Plans and the CGM Installment Balance: Representative Training
content:
# Representative training: Insulin Pump Program payment plans and the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program installment balance

**The rule taught.** The pump-plan adjustment takes off what the insulin pump program's own approved payment plan still covers, only when that program bills the same coverage record: when the pump payments posted fewer whole calendar months before today than one more than the whole calendar months since that plan was logged reach its monthly amount for each whole calendar month since it was logged, the installments it still has to collect, its installments times its monthly amount less those payments, are taken off; when that plan is behind, only its installments not yet due, the installments beyond the whole calendar months since it was logged times its monthly amount, are taken off; otherwise nothing is taken off.

The balance concerned is the plan balance of an interest-free payment plan priced on a customer's Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment.

**Q. When does this rule reach the Insulin Pump Program's plan at all?**
A. Only when the customer's Insulin Pump Program bills the same coverage record: it is not closed and its coverage record is the one the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment bills. Where it bills another coverage record, is closed, or the customer holds none, nothing is taken off.

**Q. Which plan on the Insulin Pump Program is read?**
A. The customer's Insulin Pump Program payment plan request most recently logged with status approved — an approved payment plan — with its number of monthly installments, its monthly amount and the date it was logged. Where the customer's Insulin Pump Program has no approved payment plan, nothing is taken off.

**Q. How are whole calendar months counted?**
A. Whole calendar months from one date to a later date are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's calendar day is earlier than the earlier date's calendar day. *The months since the plan was logged* are the whole calendar months from the date it was logged to today.

**Q. Which pump payments count?**
A. The patient payments posted on the customer's Insulin Pump Program billing ledger fewer whole calendar months before today than one more than the months since the plan was logged.

**Q. When is the pump plan current, and what is taken off then?**
A. It is current when those payments total at least its monthly amount multiplied by the months since it was logged. Then the installments it still has to collect are taken off: its number of installments multiplied by its monthly amount, less those payments, never below zero.

**Q. And when it is behind?**
A. When those payments fall short of that figure, only the installments not yet due are taken off: the number of installments beyond the months since it was logged (never fewer than none) multiplied by its monthly amount.

**Practice figures (hypothetical).** The customer's Insulin Pump Program bills the same coverage record as the CGM enrollment. Its approved plan of 11 installments of 47.50 was logged on 10 January; today is 20 April of the same hypothetical year, so 3 whole calendar months have passed and payments posted fewer than 4 whole calendar months before today count — a payment dated 21 December counts, one dated 20 December does not. The plan's installments multiplied by its monthly amount come to 522.50.

| Pump payments that count | Measured against 3 multiplied by 47.50, that is 142.50 | Taken off |
|---|---|---|
| 190.00 | current | 522.50 less 190.00, that is 332.50 |
| 142.50 | current | 522.50 less 142.50, that is 380.00 |
| 95.00 | behind | 11 less 3, that is 8 installments, multiplied by 47.50: 380.00 |
| 600.00 | current | 0.00 (never below zero) |

Had that behind plan been logged 13 whole calendar months ago, no installment would remain beyond those months and nothing would be taken off. Had the same Insulin Pump Program billed another coverage record, nothing would be taken off in any row.
